diffs.diff: pressure (mbar): datasheet reading gives 0.1 per count, the part's model has 1, 1
diffs.evidence: Datasheet: 'Temperature compensated pressure ... P ... 39998 ... = 3999.8 mbar' and 'P2 = (((D1*SENS2)/2^21 - OFF2)/2^13)/10 [mbar]', i.e. the compensated integer P is 0.1 mbar per count. The model applies this inside its formulas: sim solve formula ends 'P2/10' and the driver returns 'P2 / 10' (comment '# 0.1 mbar'), so the measure's scale of 1 is applied to a value already in mbar. Same conversion, expressed in different but equivalent form; the sim test (2500 mbar -> 'P=2500.0 mbar') passes.

diffs.diff: temperature (degC): datasheet reading gives 0.01 per count, the part's model has 1, 1
diffs.evidence: Datasheet: 'Actual temperature (-40...85 degC with 0.01 degC resolution) ... 1981 = 19.81 degC' and 'TEMP2 = (TEMP - Ti) / 100 [degC]', i.e. 0.01 degC per count. The model's sim solve formula ends '(TEMP - Ti)/100' and the driver returns 'TEMP2 / 100', so scale 1 is applied to a value already in degC. Equivalent units; the sim test (10 degC -> 'T=10.0 C') passes.
